home.lede: A private Nor-Tech 450 Sport, four Mercury Verado V10 425 and a professional crew. Day charters, superyacht tender service and voyages across the Caribbean arc.
home.statement: Refined comfort, a thoroughbred hull and the sea as a privilege. SARE was born for the channel between Sint Maarten and Saint-Barth, where the trade winds lift a short, steep sea and a great boat makes all the difference.
home.s1Text: Gustavia for lunch, Colombier for a swim, back in the golden hour. The islands at your own pace.
home.s2Text: The fast, dry and discreet shuttle your superyacht deserves during the high season.
home.s3Text: Island-hopping escapes from Saint-Barth to the Virgin Islands, designed around you.
home.crewText: Licensed, multilingual and at home in these waters. Our captains read the weather at dawn, book your table and know which bay will be calm by noon.
home.islands: Three islands, three nations, one day
figures: ft of carbon and hand-stitched leather
minutes from Sint Maarten to Gustavia
home.unique: The only Nor-Tech 450 Sport in Sint Maarten, Anguilla and Saint-Barth.

yacht.title: Nor-Tech 450 Sport
yacht.intro: Built to order in Minnesota by one of America's most celebrated offshore builders, the 450 Sport pairs a deep-V racing hull with the finish of a grand tourer: quilted leather, teak-effect decking, carbon console and an electric sun canopy.
yacht.pillarsTitle: Made for three kinds of day
pillars: When the Saint-Barth channel builds with the trade winds, the deep-V slices the short chop and keeps guests dry behind the console.
Bow lounge, aft benches, shade from the hardtop, swim door and ladder, a private head below. Children swim while the captain books lunch.
Coming alongside Gustavia quay or a beach club in 45 feet of gunmetal hull and four white outboards is part of the experience.
onboard: Side dive door and swim ladder
Bow lounge and twin aft benches
Spacious cabin with head, room for luggage

captions.p-helm-from-bow: From the bow to the helm
captions.stern-beach: Four Mercury outboards, anchored off Anguilla
captions.aft-deck: Dive door, open to the sea
captions.p-aft-from-helm: The aft deck from the helm
captions.p-cockpit: Teak deck and twin aft benches

charter.title: Your day, on your terms
charter.intro: Every outing is private and captained. The plan bends to the morning weather and to your mood; the chart below is where it begins.

half: Pinel, Tintamarre or Anguilla's Sandy Island. Ideal for a first outing or with children.
full: Saint-Barth, Colombier and Île Fourchue, with lunch with your feet in the sand.
transfer: Between Sint Maarten, Saint-Barth and Anguilla. From SXM, SBH or AXA airport: met on arrival, a car to the dock, then the sea. Luggage included.
sunset: Baie Longue and Terres Basses in the golden hour, before dinner ashore.

included: A professional captain and attentive service throughout the day
Still and sparkling water, sodas, fresh juices, ice and light bites
Boarding and return at Porto Cupecoy marina, or another point on request

bartender: Cocktails, chilled champagne, open bar tailored to you
clearance: Formalities and port dues, advanced by the captain

concierge: We reserve lunch at each stop
charter.chartIntro: Tap an island or an anchorage to open its guide: beaches, tables, sights and activities. Add stops to your day; distance, time and formalities update as you go.
charter.emptyDay: Add stops from the island guides.
charter.baseNote: Departure and return of every outing

personalise.title: Personalise your day
personalise.intro: Every option is arranged by our concierge and quoted on request.
cats: Dietary requirements: vegetarian, gluten-free, halal, kosher
Masks & fins for adults and children
Massage on board or on a sandbar
Pick-up from your villa or hotel
personalise.touches: Embroidered SARE towels, reef-safe sunscreen, fresh fruit and your own playlist.

occasions.title: For a special occasion
occasions.intro: Tell us what you are celebrating. We prepare the boat, the crew, the route and every detail around it.
list: Marriage proposal
Flowers, chilled champagne and the perfect cove at the perfect hour.
Wedding or vow renewal
A ceremony at sea, then a toast at anchor.
Honeymoon
A day for two, from a secluded beach to a sunset aboard.
Birthday or anniversary
Cake, champagne and the people who matter.
Sunset cruise
Baie Longue and the Terres Basses in the golden hour.
Bachelor & bachelorette
Music, cocktails and the best beach clubs of the islands.
Family day
Shallow lagoons, turtles and lunch with your feet in the sand.
Corporate & clients
Entertain your guests far from the office.
Regatta spectator
Follow the Heineken Regatta, the Bucket or Les Voiles from the water.
New Year's Eve
Watch the fireworks over Gustavia from the sea.
Scattering of ashes
A quiet, respectful farewell at sea, arranged with discretion.

stmartin.name: Saint-Martin
stmartin.blurb: Grand Case for the table, Orient Bay for the beach, Anse Marcel for a sheltered cove in the north.
stmartin.anchor: Calm anchorages in Anse Marcel and off Grand Case in settled trade winds.
beaches: The island's great beach, beach clubs and water sports.
Clear water and cliffs, snorkelling along the rocks.
Sheltered northern cove, perfect with children.
The longest sand on the island, spectacular at sunset.
dining: The island's gastronomic capital, tables at the water's edge.
French cuisine in a Creole house.
Beach club with loungers and lunch.
sights: Views over Marigot Bay and Anguilla.
Spices, crafts and island fruit, best in the morning.
Sur la trace des Arawaks museum
activities: Turtles and schools of fish off Grand Case.
Zip lines and a pool in the Pic Paradis forest.

sxm.name: Sint Maarten
sxm.blurb: The international airport, Simpson Bay lagoon and its superyacht marinas. The ideal arrival point for your guests.
sxm.anchor: Anchor off Simpson Bay, or inside the lagoon after the bridge opening.
beaches: Airliners pass just above the swimmers.
Calm turquoise water, a local favourite.
A long, quiet beach facing the anchorage.
dining: Beach bar on the sand, easy-going.
Restaurants and terraces along the boardwalk.
activities: The Flying Dutchman zip line on Sentry Hill.

pinel.name: Pinel Island
pinel.blurb: A white-sand islet minutes from Cul-de-Sac. Shallow water and lunch beneath the palms, perfect for a half day.
pinel.anchor: Nature reserve moorings on the western side, sheltered water.
beaches: Fine sand, shallow water, ideal for children.
Wilder, with views over Orient Bay.
dining: Grilled lobster and fish with your feet in the sand.
sights: A short loop with views to Tintamarre.

tintamarre.name: Tintamarre
tintamarre.blurb: A flat, uninhabited island, the wildest in the area. A deserted beach, turtles and wrecks to snorkel.
tintamarre.anchor: Moorings off Baie Blanche. No services ashore: lunch on board or at Pinel.
beaches: A long white beach, often deserted.
dining: No restaurant on the island. Bring a picnic or continue to Pinel.
sights: A relic of the days when the island had its own airline.
activities: Often grazing on the bay's seagrass.

stbarth.name: Saint-Barthélemy
stbarth.blurb: The flagship destination. Arrive at Gustavia quay, lunch at Shell Beach or Saint-Jean, swim at Colombier, reachable only by sea or on foot.
stbarth.anchor: Clearance mandatory in Gustavia. Colombier on marine reserve moorings.
beaches: Reached by sea or a trail, turtles on the seagrass.
Steps from Gustavia, a beach of tiny shells.
Wild beach and dunes, no buildings.
A cove framed by hills, superb at sunset.
dining: The hotel's table on its famous rock.
sights: Panorama over the harbour and islets.
Rue de la République and its fine boutiques.
activities: Turtles and rays in the bay.
Pain de Sucre and Les Gros Islets.

fourchue.name: Île Fourchue
fourchue.blurb: A volcanic horseshoe between Sint Maarten and Saint-Barth. A sheltered bay, crystal water, not a single building.
fourchue.anchor: Marine reserve moorings in the bay. A perfect stop on the way to Gustavia.
beaches: A small beach of pebbles and sand at the head of the bay.
dining: No services on the island. A swim stop before or after Gustavia.
sights: Bare hills and cacti, a trail to the ridges.
activities: Coral and tropical fish along the rocks.
Deep, calm water at the mooring.

anguilla.name: Anguilla
anguilla.side: Road Bay · Sandy Island · Prickly Pear
anguilla.blurb: The whitest beaches in the region, twenty minutes from Sint Maarten. Sandy Island and Prickly Pear follow clearance at Road Bay.
anguilla.anchor: Clearance at Road Bay required before Sandy Island and Prickly Pear.
beaches: A sandbar and a few palms facing Road Bay.
One of the finest beaches in the Caribbean.
Powder sand in front of the great hotels.
dining: The driftwood bar of Rendezvous Bay.
sights: Road Bay village and salt pond.

tender.title: Your yacht's tender, around the clock
tender.intro: For the length of your charter, SARE and its captain become your yacht's tender. Day and night, every journey by sea is ours: guest outings, runs to shore, transfers to the airport or another island, provisioning and errands.
tender.quote: One boat, one captain, at your yacht's side twenty-four hours a day, seven days a week.
season: Christmas and New Year in Gustavia
Les Voiles de Saint-Barth and the season's end
missions: Lunch in Anguilla, a swim at Colombier, snorkelling at Tintamarre. The yacht keeps its anchorage, your guests keep their rhythm.
Yacht to Gustavia quay, beach clubs, restaurants and villas, from breakfast to the last ride home.

Guests met on arrival at Princess Juliana (SXM), Saint-Barth (SBH) or Anguilla (AXA) airport, a car to the nearest dock with their luggage, then the sea to the yacht, their villa or the next island. The fastest way from a long-haul flight to the yacht.
Groceries, flowers, wine, urgent parts: whatever the yacht needs, fetched from Sint Maarten or Saint-Barth.
Crew changes, laundry, shopping runs and appointments ashore.
On call by VHF or WhatsApp at any hour, waiting close to the yacht.
why: Every run logged and confirmed the evening before.
Fendered approaches to swim platforms, guests stepped across hand in hand.
A deep-V offshore hull keeps guests and luggage dry, even in the channel.
No photos of guests, ever. NDAs signed on request.
formats: Seven days at your yacht's side
Event, regatta or a longer stay
tender.asideText: The rate depends on the length of the rental and your yacht's cruising area. Our concierge replies with a firm proposal.
tender.asideNote: Festive season dates go from September. Early booking guarantees availability.
how: The captain lives to your yacht's rhythm, from the first coffee run to the last shuttle home after dinner.
For the duration of the rental, SARE operates as your yacht's tender, under your yacht's insurance and alongside its crew.
One rate covers the boat and a dedicated professional captain. Nothing else to book and nothing to add.
Fuel and all other charges, such as port dues and clearance, are not included in the rate and are settled separately.
tender.seasonHint: Tap a period to see what it holds
seasonDetails: The superyachts arrive from their Atlantic crossing and take their places in Simpson Bay and Gustavia. The calmest weeks to secure a tender for the whole season.
Owners and their first guests come aboard. Booking now secures your boat and crew before the festive rush.
The busiest fortnight of the year: Gustavia's harbour is full and fireworks light the sky on New Year's Eve. Our tender is usually committed from September.
Steady trade winds, clear skies and the regatta season, from the Heineken Regatta in early March to the St. Barths Bucket later in the month.
Les Voiles de Saint-Barth and the last long days of the season, before the yachts head north.
tender.hook: Many yachts cross the Atlantic without their tender: the cost and the logistics rarely make sense. Arrive in the islands and find yours waiting.
facts: The only Nor-Tech 450 Sport in the islands
handler: One contact from the first message to the last ride home. Cédric and Rebecca answer captains, chief stewards, brokers and guests directly.

voyages.title: From Saint-Barth to the Virgin Islands
voyages.intro: Island-hopping journeys along the Caribbean arc. You sail by day at thirty-five knots and sleep ashore in the finest villas and hotels; we handle the route, fuel stops, clearances and every reservation.
how: SARE has one cabin. Your nights are spent in hand-picked villas and hotels, booked by us.
Legs are planned around the weather, with fuel stops and alternative harbours prepared in advance.
Every new island means formalities. Your captain files them ahead so you simply step ashore.
For the most distant voyages, the boat is positioned beforehand. The cost is shown in your proposal.
voyages.dreamNote: Experiences imagined to inspire; each voyage is tailored to the dates, weather and wishes of its guests.

list.name: The Northern Isles
list.teaser: Three days, four flags, and the most secret islands of the Leewards.
days: Gustavia by noon
Breakfast on Simpson Bay, lunch on Shell Beach, an afternoon swim with the turtles of Colombier. Dinner in Gustavia, a suite on the hill above the harbour.
Saba, the unspoiled queen

A green volcano rising from the sea. Drop into the marine park's pinnacles, then lunch in Windwardside. In the afternoon, Statia's Oranje Bay and the crater of The Quill. Night at a plantation inn on Nevis.
Brimstone Hill and home
Morning at the great fortress of St Kitts, a last swim at Cockleshell Bay with the Narrows stretching to Nevis, then a long golden crossing back to Sint Maarten.

list.name: The Virgin Islands Run
list.region: Anegada · Virgin Gorda · Jost Van Dyke
list.teaser: The Anegada Passage, where a deep-V hull shows what it was built for.
days: Across the Anegada Passage
Eighty miles of open Atlantic swell, crossed at speed and in comfort. Land on Anegada's endless flats for lobster grilled in half-barrels on Loblolly Bay.
The Baths
Morning among the granite boulders and turquoise pools of Virgin Gorda, before the day-trippers arrive. Lunch in North Sound, sunset over the reefs.
Jost Van Dyke
White Bay at its most beautiful: swim ashore to the bar that invented the Painkiller, then lose an afternoon on Sandy Spit, a sand islet with a single palm.
Norman Island and back
Snorkel the caves of Norman Island, said to have hidden pirate treasure, then fly home across the Passage.

list.name: Antigua & Barbuda
list.teaser: Nelson's harbour, a pink beach that runs for seventeen miles, and Sunday at Shirley Heights.
days: English Harbour
Arrive in the Georgian dockyard where Nelson's fleet was careened. Superyachts alongside, dinner in a stone boathouse by candlelight.
Barbuda's pink sands
A beach of pink-tinted sand without a footprint, and the frigate birds of Codrington Lagoon puffing out their scarlet throats.
Shirley Heights
A slow morning in Carlisle Bay, then sunset above English Harbour as the steel band plays and the whole island seems to arrive.
Return by Montserrat
Pass beneath the smoking volcano of Montserrat and its buried capital, a sight you will not forget, then home.

list.name: French Antilles to the Grenadines
list.region: Guadeloupe · Dominica · Martinique · Saint Lucia · Grenadines
list.teaser: Eight nights down the volcanic spine of the Caribbean, to the turtles of the Tobago Cays.
days: Les Saintes
Guadeloupe's tiny archipelago, one of the world's most beautiful bays. Bicycles, red roofs and the Fort Napoléon at sunset.
Dominica, the nature island
Rivers through the rainforest, hot springs and, offshore, sperm whales that live here all year.
Martinique
The Anses d'Arlet, Diamond Rock rising from the sea, and an evening at a rum distillery among the sugar cane.
The Pitons
Anchor between the twin peaks of Saint Lucia, a UNESCO site. Dinner looking up at the Gros Piton under the stars.
Bequia and Mustique
The boatbuilders of Bequia, then lunch at a legendary bar on Mustique, the island of discreet celebrities.
Tobago Cays
Swim with green turtles in the most perfect lagoon of the Grenadines, then a lobster barbecue on the beach of Petit Bateau.

list.name: The Exumas, Bahamas
list.region: Nassau · Allan's Cay · Staniel Cay · Harbour Island
list.teaser: Three hundred and sixty-five cays, sandbars that appear at low tide, and water in colours you did not know existed.
days: Into the Exumas
From Nassau to Allan's Cay and its prehistoric iguanas. The water turns from sapphire to the palest jade as the banks rise beneath the hull.
Thunderball Grotto
Swim into the domed cave where a James Bond film was shot, light falling through the roof onto the fish.
The swimming pigs
The famous pigs of Big Major Cay paddle out to greet you, then lunch at the Staniel Cay Yacht Club.
The sandbars
A private sandbar that exists only at low tide: a table set in the middle of the sea, just for you.
Harbour Island
Pink sand, pastel cottages and golf carts. Dinner at one of the most elegant small hotels in the Caribbean.

voyages.formIntro: Tell us the islands that make you dream, your dates and your party. We reply with a route, a schedule of nights ashore and a complete proposal.

further.title: Further afield, on request
further.intro: With the boat positioned beforehand, we also design escapes to the Grenadines, to Martinique and Saint Lucia, and to the Exumas.

crew.title: A fleet of professionals, one standard
crew.intro: SARE is a concierge house. Behind every outing stands a pool of licensed captains, hostesses and bartenders, chosen for your day, your language and your occasion, and held to one standard of safety and discretion.
crew.captainText: Commercially licensed and trained in safety and first aid, our captains run these waters every day of the season. For each booking we assign the crew best suited to it: the route, the languages spoken aboard, the occasion. Cédric and Rebecca remain your single point of contact from the first message to the last ride home.
standards: Life jackets, emergency procedures and swimming rules explained at boarding, in your language.
Forecast and sea state checked at dawn. If the channel is too rough, we propose a calmer plan before you leave home.
Engine hours logged, a service before every season, a boat cleaned and prepared before each outing.
Commercial charter insurance, licensed vessel and safety equipment inspected.
No photos of guests on social media. Confidentiality agreements signed on request.
Chilled towels, cold drinks, reservations confirmed: the details that make a day effortless.
day: Weather check and a call to confirm your plan
Welcome aboard, safety briefing, chilled towels
Lunch ashore, table reserved by your captain
Snorkelling, paddle or a siesta under the canopy

clearance.title: Several nations in a single day
clearance.intro: Saint-Martin, Sint Maarten, Saint-Barthélemy and Anguilla belong to three different countries. Every border crossing goes through customs. Your captain handles it; here is what concerns you. The territories on your plan are highlighted.

fr.name: Saint-Martin
items: Departures and returns within the French side need no formalities.
Declarations are filed online or at a kiosk before changing territory.
Nature reserve at Pinel and Tintamarre: moorings only, no anchoring on seagrass.

nl.name: Sint Maarten
items: Entry and exit at Simpson Bay or Great Bay on the same day.
Port and lagoon bridge fees depending on the anchorage.
Boarding on the Dutch side is ideal for arrivals at SXM airport.
nl.fee: Port and bridge fees depending on route

bl.name: Saint-Barthélemy
items: Gustavia is the island's only port of entry.
Customs form and port form completed online before arrival.
Port dues by boat length and berth: quay or anchorage.
Marine reserve: Colombier and Île Fourchue on moorings.

ai.name: Anguilla
items: Clear in at Road Bay before any stop at Sandy Island or Prickly Pear.
Foreign charter boats pay entry charges and per-passenger taxes.
Exact quote sent 48 hours ahead, based on the number of guests.
ai.fee: Charter dues + passenger taxes, on quote

clearance.voyagesText: Each new island or nation means an entry and an exit, and some countries such as the Bahamas require a cruising permit. Your captain prepares every formality ahead and the fees appear in your proposal.
checklist: A valid passport for every guest, children included, as soon as the day leaves the French side of Saint-Martin.
Names, dates of birth, nationalities and passport numbers let us file the declarations online before departure.
Port dues, clearance fees and entry charges are advanced by the captain and re-invoiced without margin, receipts provided.
clearance.legal: Procedures and amounts change with port authorities and the season. This information is indicative and confirmed by the captain when you book.

ui.goodTitle: Good to know before you sail
ui.waMsg: Hello SARE, I would like some information about a day charter / tender.

explore.title: Three islands at our door, a whole sea beyond
explore.intro: Start with the three islands we sail every day, then pull back to the whole Caribbean. Tap any island to discover what not to miss.

stmartin.name: Saint-Martin · Sint Maarten
stmartin.tagline: One island, two nations and our home port: French tables on one side, superyacht marinas on the other.
must: The island's gastronomic street, tables right above the water.
The great beach of the north-east, with its beach clubs and turquoise lagoon.
Two protected islets: lunch under the palms, then turtles over the seagrass.
Airliners skim the swimmers on their final approach to SXM.
Spices, rum and island fruit, best on a Wednesday or Saturday morning.

stbarth.name: Saint-Barthélemy
stbarth.tagline: The Caribbean's most elegant island, thirty minutes from our dock.
must: Come alongside the quay among the superyachts, then stroll the boutiques of Rue de la République.
A cove reached only by sea or on foot, where turtles graze below the hull.
Feet in the sand on a beach of tiny shells, a step from the harbour.
Wild dunes and not a building in sight, the island at its purest.
Fireworks over a harbour packed with the world's finest yachts.

anguilla.name: Anguilla
anguilla.tagline: The whitest sand in the region and a calm, unhurried luxury, twenty minutes away.
must: A sandbar with a few palms and grilled lobster, facing Road Bay.
Remote cays with crystal water and shallow reefs to snorkel.
Two miles of powder sand, often called one of the world's finest beaches.
The driftwood bar of reggae legend Bankie Banx on Rendezvous Bay.
The national sport: locally built sloops racing in summer regattas.

saba.name: Saba
saba.tagline: A green volcano rising straight from the sea, the unspoiled queen of the Caribbean.
must: Climb through cloud forest to the highest point of the Kingdom of the Netherlands.
Dive the pinnacles, seamounts covered in coral and pelagic life.
A single road built by hand over decades, winding from the sea to the villages.
White cottages with green shutters and red roofs, lunch with a view.
A delicate needlework tradition kept alive by the island's women.

statia.name: Sint Eustatius · Statia
statia.tagline: A quiet island with a great past and a perfect volcanic crater.
must: Hike into the crater of a dormant volcano, filled with rainforest.
Where the first salute to the American flag was fired in 1776.
Dive the submerged warehouses of the once-busiest port in the Caribbean.
A dark-sand bay beneath the cliffs of Oranjestad.
The island's history in an eighteenth-century merchant's house.

stkitts.name: St Kitts & Nevis
stkitts.country: Federation of St Kitts and Nevis
stkitts.tagline: Two volcanic islands, a great fortress and the old plantation inns of Nevis.
must: A UNESCO World Heritage fortress with views across to Saba and Statia.
The old sugar train circling St Kitts, with a drink on the open deck.
A calm beach facing The Narrows and the cone of Nevis Peak.
Long golden sand, palm trees and a famous beach bar.
Birthplace of Alexander Hamilton, now a small museum.

antigua.name: Antigua & Barbuda
antigua.tagline: Nelson's harbour, three hundred and sixty-five beaches and a pink island next door.
must: The Georgian naval dockyard at English Harbour, a UNESCO site.
Steel band and sunset above English Harbour.
A protected crescent of sand on the wild Atlantic coast.
Seventeen miles of pink-tinted sand without a footprint.
Thousands of frigate birds in Codrington Lagoon, males puffing scarlet throats.

montserrat.name: Montserrat
montserrat.tagline: The emerald isle of the Caribbean, shaped by its living volcano.
must: Watch the steaming dome from a safe viewpoint.
The former capital, buried in ash, seen from the boat.
Scientists explain the eruptions that reshaped the island.
The island's only white-sand beach, reached by sea.
Shamrocks on passports and a St Patrick's festival unique in the Caribbean.

guadeloupe.name: Guadeloupe
guadeloupe.tagline: A butterfly of two islands, with Les Saintes and Marie-Galante as its jewels.
must: One of the world's most beautiful bays, red roofs and Fort Napoléon.
Diving and snorkelling around the Pigeon Islets.
Ox carts, white beaches and some of the finest agricultural rums in the world.
Waterfalls tumbling from the slopes of La Soufrière.
Cliffs at the eastern tip where the Atlantic meets the Caribbean Sea.

dominica.name: Dominica
dominica.tagline: The nature island: rainforest, rivers and whales that live here all year.
must: A resident family of sperm whales just off the west coast.
Snorkel through curtains of warm volcanic bubbles.
Twin waterfalls with hot springs at their foot.
A silent rowing-boat trip beneath mangroves and swamp bloodwood.
A long rainforest hike to a flooded fumarole, for the adventurous.

martinique.name: Martinique
martinique.tagline: The island of flowers, of rum and of the Diamond Rock.
must: A fishing village, a white church on the beach and turtles in the bay.
A rock that served as a Royal Navy ship, an extraordinary dive.
Rum cellars, a Creole mansion and a contemporary art park.
The old capital destroyed in 1902, beneath its volcano.
Waist-deep white sand among the islets of Le François, with a planter's punch.

stlucia.name: Saint Lucia
stlucia.tagline: Two volcanic spires rising from the sea and the most romantic bays in the Caribbean.
must: Anchor between Gros Piton and Petit Piton, a UNESCO site.
A drive-in volcano with warm mineral mud baths.
A hurricane hole fringed with palms, one of the loveliest anchorages anywhere.
Snorkelling on a reef that starts at the water's edge.
Fort ruins and views over Rodney Bay.

grenadines.name: The Grenadines
grenadines.tagline: A string of small islands, each more beautiful than the last.
must: Swim with green turtles in a lagoon of impossible blues.
The island of discreet celebrities, and a sundowner at Basil's Bar.
Admiralty Bay, Princess Margaret Beach and the island's model boat builders.
A perfect crescent of sand and palms.
A private-island resort with flags to call for room service.

grenada.name: Grenada
grenada.tagline: The spice island: nutmeg, rainforest and a harbour of painted houses.
must: Statues on the seabed of Molinere Bay, slowly turning to coral.
Two miles of white sand facing St George's.
Nutmeg, cocoa and cinnamon, and chocolate made on the spot.
A rum distillery still driven by a water wheel.
St George's horseshoe harbour, one of the prettiest in the Caribbean.

barbados.name: Barbados
barbados.tagline: English elegance in the Caribbean, alone in the Atlantic to the east.
must: Snorkel over shipwrecks with turtles in Bridgetown's bay.
The wild Atlantic coast and its giant rocks.
A rum tasting with one of the world's oldest rum houses.
The island's fish fry, music and dancing by the sea.
The old town and the Garrison, a UNESCO site.

bvi.name: British Virgin Islands
bvi.tagline: Sixty islands and cays, the most famous sailing waters in the world.
must: Giant granite boulders and turquoise pools on Virgin Gorda.
Swim ashore to the bar that invented the Painkiller.
Endless flats, flamingos and lobster on Loblolly Bay.
A sand islet with a single palm tree.
A Victorian steamship wreck, one of the Caribbean's great dives.

usvi.name: US Virgin Islands
usvi.tagline: National park beaches on St John, and the reefs of St Croix.
must: An underwater snorkelling trail in a national park bay.
Most of St John is protected forest and coves.
A national monument reef off St Croix.
Danish colonial streets and duty-free shopping.

puertorico.name: Puerto Rico · Culebra & Vieques
puertorico.tagline: Spanish islands of the east, wild beaches and a glowing bay.
must: A horseshoe of white sand regularly ranked among the world's best.
A bioluminescent bay that glows blue with every movement.
Colourful streets and the fortress of El Morro, a UNESCO site.
The only tropical rainforest in the US national forest system.
A sandy cay off Fajardo with clear, shallow water.

turks.name: Turks & Caicos
turks.tagline: Water so clear it seems to vanish, and one of the world's great beaches.
must: Twelve miles of soft white sand on Providenciales.
A lagoon of an almost unreal turquoise, dotted with tiny islets.
Little Water Cay and its protected rock iguanas.
A drop-off plunging thousands of feet just offshore.
From January to April the whales pass through to calve.

bahamas.name: The Bahamas · Exumas
bahamas.tagline: Three hundred and sixty-five cays and water in colours you did not know existed.
must: The famous pigs of Big Major Cay paddle out to greet you.
Swim into the domed cave where a James Bond film was shot.
Private sandbars that appear only at low tide.
Pink sand beaches and pastel cottages.
Prehistoric-looking rock iguanas on a tiny cay.

faq.title: Before you come aboard
items: What is included in a day charter?
Your captain and his service, fuel for the agreed programme, soft drinks and snacks, with boarding and return at Porto Cupecoy marina. Another pick-up point can be arranged.
Do my guests need passports?
Yes. Saint-Martin, Sint Maarten, Saint-Barth and Anguilla belong to three different countries, so every guest, children included, needs a valid passport for most itineraries.
Who takes care of customs and clearance?
Our concierge. We ask for the guest list 48 hours ahead and file every declaration. Port dues and clearance fees are re-invoiced at cost, with receipts.
What if the weather turns?
Your captain checks the forecast and the sea at dawn. If conditions are not right, we propose a calmer route or another date.
Can children come aboard?
Of course. Child life jackets are on board. Simply tell us their ages when you book.
What should we bring?
Swimwear, reef-safe sunscreen, a hat and passports. Towels, snorkelling gear and cold drinks are waiting on board.
How do I pay?
Once we confirm the date, you receive a secure payment link. Nothing is charged before that.
How does the tender service work?
For superyachts only: the boat and a dedicated captain at your yacht's disposal around the clock, under your yacht's insurance. Fuel and other charges are not included.
